stemMd: There are 30 people at a meeting. Eighteen speak French, 17 speak German, and everyone speaks at least one of the two. How many speak both?
explanationMd: Adding language counts gives 35, but only 30 people exist and nobody speaks neither. The excess five are counted twice, so five speak both. This is inclusion-exclusion: 18 + 17 − both = 30.

distractorRationale.d: This is the number speaking French but not German.
distractorRationale.c: This is the number speaking German but not French.
distractorRationale.a: This uses the difference between language counts rather than their overlap.
